findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only) - False positive. The 'xmpp' string appears in DOMPurify library's URI scheme whitelist regex allowing xmpp: protocol links in sanitized HTML. No XMPP message data is collected or transmitted by the application.
findings.evidence: purify.es-CC4Brkr_.js line ~2 (byte offset 10325): DOMPurify URI scheme whitelist regex includes 'xmpp' as an allowed protocol. This is part of the DOMPurify library (a third-party HTML sanitizer) and does not indicate any actual XMPP message collection, processing, or transmission by the application.
findings.recommendation: No action needed. This is a false positive from the DOMPurify library. If the app ever implements actual XMPP messaging, ensure appropriate Play Store Data Safety declarations and prominent disclosure are added.
findings.purpose: No collection - false positive in DOMPurify URI scheme whitelist

findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only) - React internal error handler found but no off-device crash reporting SDK (Sentry, Firebase Crashlytics, etc.) is configured. Error is only logged locally via console.error.
findings.evidence: index-BMHFFNQZ.js at byte 38750: React internal polyfill code contains 'process.emit("uncaughtException", e)' followed by 'console.error(e)'. No crash reporting SDK dependencies found in package.json. No google-services.json found. The error handler is React's internal mechanism that logs errors locally via console.error.
findings.recommendation: No immediate action needed. If a crash reporting service (e.g., Firebase Crashlytics, Sentry) is added in the future, the developer must: (1) declare crash log collection in the Play Store Data Safety form, (2) add prominent in-app disclosure with affirmative consent before crash data transmission begins.
findings.purpose: Local error handling only - React internal polyfill
